Pittari for iPhone · Support

Every ticket, framed just right.

Pittari (ぴったり, “just right”) finds the codes in your ticket PDFs and screenshots, redraws them sharp and keeps them ready to scan. Free, with no ads, no subscription and no account needed.

Add a ticketThe check markAt the doorWidgets and moreApple WalletCardsContact

Add a ticket

  • Share it. In Mail, Files or Photos, share the ticket’s PDF or a screenshot and choose Pittari.
  • Or add it in the app. Tap + and choose a PDF or image, or a picture from Photos.
  • Just looking? Try a Sample Ticket opens a made-up concert ticket, and About imports a made-up trip with three codes.

Pittari reads QR, Aztec, PDF417, Data Matrix and the common barcodes. Each code becomes its own pass, and Pittari fills in the event, date, venue and seat from the ticket’s text, in English or Spanish. Airline boarding passes give the flight, route and seat. Check the review and Save; Edit on a pass changes anything later.

The check mark

QR, Aztec and PDF417 codes are redrawn from their own data, so they stay crisp at any size. Pittari then reads the redrawn code back and compares it with the original. The check mark means they say exactly the same thing.

When Pittari can’t confirm a redraw, or the code is a kind it doesn’t redraw, it keeps the code as it appears in the file, cropped with a clean white margin. You can switch between Redrawn and Original on any pass.

At the door

Show Code puts the code full screen with the brightness all the way up, and your iPhone stays awake while it’s up. Close gives your brightness back.

A pass with a date leads the list until its event ends: three hours after it starts, unless you set an end.

Without opening the app

  • Next Pass widget for the Home Screen and the Lock Screen.
  • Show Next Pass in Control Center or on the Action button.
  • Pin to Lock Screen on a pass keeps it on the Lock Screen and in the Dynamic Island as a Live Activity.
  • Siri and Shortcuts: “Show my next pass in Pittari”, and Import Codes From a File for your own shortcuts.

Apple Wallet

On a pass, tap Apple Wallet. The first time, link Pittari with Sign in with Apple: Pittari asks Apple for no name and no email. Then tap Add to Apple Wallet. Pittari signs the pass, and Wallet shows Pittari as the one who issued it.

Each pass you add is kept for a year, with room for 50, sealed on your iPhone so only your devices can open it. In About, Kept Passes, keep a pass another year, add it to Wallet again, restore it on a new iPhone, or delete it to make room. Your iPhones share the kept passes through iCloud Keychain, which must be on for each of them.

Wallet’s own Create a Pass, on iOS 27, can also make a pass from the pass picture: save it from the Apple Wallet screen, then add it from Photos. It is Apple’s feature: it needs an iPhone with Apple Intelligence and isn’t available everywhere.

To leave, use About, Delete Account: every kept pass is deleted, and Apple is asked to forget Pittari’s link with your Apple Account.

Your card, in Wallet’s new style

On iOS 27, Wallet shows membership, loyalty and gift cards as a card with artwork. On the Apple Wallet screen, tap Make It a Card. A store card you made from a photo or screenshot is already offered as a card made from that picture, with its colors, its logo and the picture itself: tap Design the Card to change it. Design the Card has twelve templates and eleven patterns, and cuts the logo and artwork from your card’s picture. iPhones before iOS 27 show the classic pass, with the same logo and colors.

To change a pass later, tap the pencil on it. Edit Pass starts with its look (Card Design for a card), then its name, details, code, date and place, and notes.

What if Pittari’s server goes away?

Your passes don’t depend on it. Passes already in Apple Wallet keep working: Wallet never asks Pittari about them. The passes in Pittari live on your iPhone and show full screen, in widgets and on the Lock Screen with or without the server; adding new ones to Wallet is what needs it.

If the server ever loses your kept passes, link with Apple again if Pittari asks you to: each iPhone then keeps its own passes again by itself, for the rest of their year. A pass whose only copy was the kept one, from an iPhone you no longer have, can’t come back.

Nobody can read your kept passes on the server, even someone who broke in: each one is sealed on your iPhone with a key that stays in your iCloud Keychain.

Your tickets stay with you

Finding codes and reading tickets happens on your iPhone, and your passes stay there. A place search you ask for in the editor goes to Apple Maps, and Apple Wallet goes through Pittari’s backend, which can’t read the passes it keeps for you. The privacy policy has the details.

Contact

Questions, problems or a ticket Pittari can’t read: support@neorgon.org.

Please don’t send a ticket that’s still valid: its code is the ticket. A screenshot of the problem with the code covered is enough.

Pittari needs an iPhone with iOS 18 or later, and speaks English and Spanish.
